questions.stem: Why is cellulose not digestible by humans, even though it is made from glucose like starch?

options.text: Cellulose contains different elements than starch
Humans lack the enzyme needed to break the bonds between beta-glucose units in cellulose

questions.explanation: Both starch and cellulose are made from glucose, but they use different forms: starch uses alpha-glucose and cellulose uses beta-glucose. The bonds between beta-glucose units in cellulose are arranged differently, and humans do not produce an enzyme capable of breaking them. Cellulose passes through as dietary fibre.
